sentences.text: The holotype specimen SPG 1912 VIII 177 — the specific fossil the species is based on — is a thick-skulled cranium characterized by small dorsotemporal fossae.
Only one species, Aegyptosuchus peyeri, has been described for this genus found in the Bahariya Formation of Egypt.
Aegyptosuchus is notable for its thick cranial roof.
Aegyptosuchus fossils were discovered in the Bahariya Formation of Egypt from the Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous.
Additional fossil remains including teeth and various vertebrae were lost during World War II bombings of Munich.
The genus Aegyptosuchus was named by Stromer in 1933.
Aegyptosuchus belongs to the family Aegyptosuchidae, which also includes the genus Aegisuchus.
The family Aegyptosuchidae is part of the clade Eusuchia and is considered the sister group to the crown group Crocodylia.
Carroll classified the genus Aegyptosuchus into the family Stomatosuchidae in 1988.
Holliday and Gardner reclassified Aegyptosuchus into the family Aegyptosuchidae in 2012, viewing it as distinct from stomatosuchids and closely related to Aegisuchus.
Aegyptosuchus lived during the Cenomanian stage, between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
